claims.text: All of the scoring runs in the browser, in plain, unminified `https://all22pokemon.com/draft.js` (last modified 2026-10-14) [1].
It is `100 × Σ(role weight × normalized stat)`, plus the largest type bonus among the Pokémon's types (2–6 points), clamped to 0–100 [1].
HP runs 20–150, Atk/Def/SpA/SpD run 20–140, and Spe runs 20–130 [1].
BST (base stat total) is not used [1].
**How the team is scored.** `raw = 0.82 × (offense weighted avg + defense weighted avg)/2 + 0.18 × mean(4 lowest fits of all 22 starters)` [1].
There is no team-synergy type bonus [1].
Each round rolls a region uniformly at random, then a type that region still has [1][2].
The placement is final [1][2].
Each run has exactly **one type reroll and one region reroll** in total, and a run allows at most 3 Legendaries [1][2].
**Saved state.** The current run is stored in localStorage under `pokemon-all22-draft-v1`, and lifetime stats under `pokemon-all22-draft-stats-v1` [2].

claims.section: Per-position stat weights and type bonuses (from `ROLES` in draft.js)
claims.text: The bonus is added after the stat sum and before the 0–100 clamp [1].
The displayed offense and defense sub-scores use each side's 2 weakest spots instead, but the Team Score comes only from `raw` [1].
Fits are rounded only for display (`app.js`) [1].
The variant passed in is `draft.variant` (`all` or `retro`) [1].
A code comment says the curves were "Calibrated on the real results of ~57,000 seasons (October 2026) ... about 0.1% of teams reach 950 and about 0.01% reach 1000" [1].
**Slot importance weights** (each side sums to 1) [1]:
Above 950, one raw point is worth about 20 score points in "all" and about 33 in retro [1].
Only the scoring role changes, through `SCHEME_ROLE = { "43": { NT: "DT", ILB2: "DT", ILB1: "MLB" }, slot: { FB: "SLOT" } }` [1][2].
Formations are chosen before the run and locked once it starts, and the challenge has no kicker [2][5].
The `/draft` page is a different game: a multiplayer Fantasy Draft [2].
The pool variants are `all: GENS` and `retro: ["1","2","3","4"]` [1][2].
A separate "151 Challenge" rolls a single Kanto Pokémon each round, has 5 rerolls and uses its own curve [1][2].
**Rounds:** `ROUNDS = 22` [2].
A roll is therefore never empty [2].
(Inference, from the researcher's reading of the code) Rolls are not weighted by how many Pokémon a region or type has [2].
**Eligible picks:** any Pokémon in `POOL[gen]` that isn't taken, isn't a Legendary once the cap is used, and has the rolled type as either of its types [2].
Duplicates are impossible [2].
Once the cap is reached, rolls never land on a region and type that only has Legendaries left [2].
That is one of each per run, and they cost nothing beyond using them up [2].
**Signed-out runs:** the rolls are deterministic from the stored `seed`, including rerolls (`seed ^ 0x2e7011` / `seed ^ 0x6e9e11`) [2].
The server deals them through `/api/app?a=...`, the seed is kept secret, and moves must be at least 1000 ms apart [2].
The prefix is `"pokemon-all22"` [2][4].
| `pokemon-all22-draft-stats-v1` | `{runs, perfect, bestScore, bestWins}` (synced to the account [8]) |
No IndexedDB use was found [2].
The example values are reconstructed [2]:
Signed-in runs drop `seed` and add `id`, `step`, `uid`, `result`, `post` and `shiny` [2].
There is no JSON file [3][4].
**`pokedata.js` [3]:** one string per Pokémon, `"types|HP,Atk,Def,SpA,SpD,Spe|weightKg"`.
**`pokemon.js` [4]:** `POKEMON_NAMES`, `HEIGHT_DM` (decimeters), the `LEGENDARIES` set, and `GEN_ENDS = [151,251,386,493,649,721,809,905,1025]`.

The functions are pure. `DRAFT.positionScore(id, slot, scheme)` and `DRAFT.teamScore(lineup, scheme, variant)` depend only on these globals, so a bot can load the three files and call them directly [1].
**How many rerolls.** Heldgames says "You get up to five rerolls for the whole draft" [9].
The site's code gives the 17–0 run `rerolls: { type: 1, gen: 1 }` [2], and the 5 belongs to the separate 151 Challenge (`MON_REROLLS = 5`) [1].
**How the weak-spot penalty is described.** The homepage says "your four weakest spots drag the whole team down" [6].
The code implements this as an 18% blend toward the mean of the 4 lowest fits, not as a subtraction [1].
It probably shares draft.js ("Pure game logic (no DOM), so it can also be simulated outside the browser") [1][2].
Re-fetch it before relying on these numbers [1].
**No community strategy material.** There's no public repo [7].
The site launched around 2026-10-09 [10].
The creator (@ColeThereum) and the Discord (discord.gg/B8YvRMtrVt) need a logged-in human to read [7].
